candidates.title: An optimized power conversion system for a stellarator-based nuclear fusion power plant
candidates.notes: Famà et al. 2023, Energy Conversion and Management. Reports 51% PCS efficiency and 34% net electrical efficiency, but for a liquid metal wall stellarator at 700–900°C with sCO2 Brayton-Rankine cycle — not the WCLL/EUROFER97 Stellaris configuration. Scheduled open archive Dec 18, 2024, but extraction still returned paywall shell only. Removed after failed extraction.

candidates.title: First considerations on the Balance of Plant for a HELIAS fusion power plant
candidates.notes: Fusion Engineering and Design, 2019. Uses HCPB blanket with helium cooling and solar salt intermediate loop (not WCLL). Thermal efficiency presented as a range (35–70%) for sensitivity analysis, not a design-point value. Paywalled — abstract only accessible. Not extracted.

candidates.title: Fusion for high-value heat production
candidates.notes: Economic/policy analysis of heat vs. electricity commercialization strategy. Does not contain thermal efficiency specifications or power conversion cycle data. Skipped.

failed.reason: Paywall shell only — extraction returned empty section headers with no quantitative content. File removed. Note: open archive date was Dec 18, 2024 (past), but ScienceDirect extraction still failed to retrieve full text.

gaps_attempted.notes: No new open-access source found specifically addressing WCLL steam Rankine thermal efficiency for a stellarator. The HELIAS BoP paper (2019, HCPB configuration) and the Famà et al. power conversion paper (liquid metal wall, sCO2) are the closest available analogues but are paywalled and/or wrong configuration. The existing sources arxiv-1401-4232 (general fusion conversion) and helios-stellarator-comparison.md (40% for vanadium-alloy Helios) remain the best proxies. The ~32% efficiency inferred from EUROFER97 temperature limits is analytically grounded but still lacks a direct primary citation for the WCLL-steam Rankine specific case.

candidates.title: Coil geometry with large openings for a HSR3-like stellarator reactor for fast replacement of in-vessel components
candidates.notes: Queral et al., Jan 2025. HSR3 (3 field periods, HELIAS-type stellarator reactor). Discusses coil geometry modifications for maintenance access. Abstract states: blanket/divertor replacement every 1–4 years; proposes coils located far from plasma at outboard region to create wide maintenance openings. Does NOT provide specific coil count or per-coil mass. Full PDF extraction failed (rc=1, no stderr). Extracted abstract page only.

candidates.title: Designing Coils for Compact Stellarators
candidates.notes: OSTI COILOPT paper. Search snippet mentioned exploring coil numbers between 3–7 per half-field period using ARIES-CS scale as reference. May contain coil count ranges but not per-coil mass data. Not extracted due to budget constraints.

extracted.notes: Abstract-only extraction (trafilatura got landing page, not full PDF). Contains: blanket/divertor module replacement interval 1–4 years (important for replacement scheme component of G-11), HSR3 coil geometry description, context on modular coil maintenance access approach. Does not satisfy coil count or per-coil mass components of G-11.

gaps_attempted.notes: Blanket replacement interval (1–4 years per Queral et al. 2025) now partially sourced for the 'replacement scheme' component of G-11. Coil count and per-coil mass remain not-yet-sourced. The Stellaris paper §2.11 (remote maintenance) is the authoritative source but existing extraction may not have captured that section's quantitative detail. summary.notes: G-4 remains unaddressed by new sources — WCLL-specific thermal efficiency requires either the full Stellaris paper or a DEMO WCLL power conversion study (both paywalled or not yet found). G-11 partially addressed — replacement interval sourced from arXiv:2501.04640 abstract, but coil count and per-coil mass still not sourced. The sCO2 Brayton-Rankine stellarator paper (Famà et al. 2023) is a potential high-value source for G-4 context once full text is accessible; scheduled open archive date has passed but extraction pipeline still returned paywall shell.
